side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard).
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame
note: The outer nonce is SHA-256(label, link_id, link_seq) with no stream id in it. One counter per link gives distinct nonces across the streams of a link; one counter per (link, stream), each starting at 0, gives two streams on one link the same outer nonce, and a receiver built the other way cannot open. The nonce formula supports per link; the loss-recovery paragraph is written per (link, stream).

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 is a 64-byte Ed25519 signature by the bound chunk key, appended to the inner unit after the inner ciphertext and inside the outer seal
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 the shipping form, which precedes the signature with an 8-byte publisher timestamp `source_ms` under the domain `ciris-edge:av-chunk-sig:v2`
note: One sentence lays out the v1 trailer (64 bytes, domain av-chunk-sig:v1) and says the shipping form is another (72 bytes, domain v2, budget eight bytes lower) without laying it out. The relay rule still reads "take the last 64 bytes as the trailer". An implementer of the written layout and one of the shipping form refuse each other's chunks as av_chunk_trailer_invalid. CC 2.6.1.8 only says the trailer stays a raw signature.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 are the only shapes this Part registers
side_b: CC 3.4.11 provider/government rungs MAY further qualify `{level}` with a `{verifier_key}` / `{credential_class}`
note: Same sentence. The registry and the match vectors carry only age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version}; age_assurance: is a reserved stem, so CC 3.1.7 refuses an unclaimed leaf under it as namespace_family_unregistered. A producer using the MAY emits a row every conformant substrate refuses. The registry supports "only two shapes".

side_a: CC 3.4.11 Parsers MUST tolerate the trailing `:vN` version segment.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 A dimension without it is refused with **`missing_version_segment`**, never admitted as a second leaf beside its versioned sibling.
note: Tolerate reads as optional; CC 3.1.7 and the code block of CC 3.4.11 itself ("is mandatory") require the segment, and the vectors refuse age_assurance:provider:minor without it. CC 3.1.7 governs.

side_a: CC 6.1.1 **Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule).
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)
note: Two orders named as one rule. Byte order over UTF-8 and UTF-16 code-unit order differ for ids holding a supplementary character beside one in U+E000 to U+FFFF, so two builders compute different roots. CC 6.1.2.1.2 ("raw leaf bytes") and CC 6.1.5.2 ("over UTF-8 bytes") support byte order for the binary preimages; the citation of the JCS set rule is the odd one. CC 3.2 sorts a recovery commitment array "by key_id as UTF-8 bytes" inside JCS, the same split.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.1.1 public keys, `destination_hash`, `root_hash`, digests and fingerprints — MUST be lowercase hex per [CC 2.6.3](#2.6.3)
side_b: CC 3.2 Each entry's three members are exactly as stored on the key record (`pubkey_*_base64`, standard base64).
note: The general rule names public keys as hex, "never base64 in canonical bytes"; the key record (signed_object.tsv: pubkey_ed25519_base64, pubkey_ml_dsa_65_base64), the recovery commitment, encryption_pubkeys and onion_hop_pubkeys carry public keys as base64 inside signed bytes. The next sentence of 2.6.1.1.1 lets a field definition say base64, so a careful reader follows the field; the list of examples in the rule is wrong for most public keys.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.5 the contract; forward the octets as received)
side_b: CC 2.6.1.3 [CC 2.6.1.1](#2.6.1.1) requires it to re-canonicalize member order while holding member presence/absence fixed.
note: CC 2.6.1.1 requires JCS only of a relay "that re-serializes from a parsed object at all"; CC 2.6.1.3 reads it as a duty on every relay that re-emits, and concludes the received octets are the canonical ones. A relay forwarding a pretty-printed envelope verbatim follows 2.6.1.1, 2.6.1.4 and 2.6.1.5 and breaks the premise of 2.6.1.3. Signatures verify either way.

side_a: CC 3.3.2 The wrap is `wrap_algorithm` (v2 only) and `wrapped_dek`.
side_b: CC 3.3.2 Both rows above are the frozen snake_case forms.
note: The closed set has two rows (v1 and v2) and decode is "reject an unknown string", so v1 is a known string; the key-grant paragraph, CC 5.1 ("never `v1`") and CC 4.4.3.4.1 make v1 a refusal on every wrap this document describes. The table's v2 row scopes the mandate to "streaming epoch-DEK grants" only, narrower than CC 5.1 ("A DEK that is wrapped MUST be wrapped with v2").

side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 hard ceiling 2³²−1 chunks per epoch
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 it MUST stay below 2³² within an epoch, the 5.3.3.1 ceiling
note: A counter below 2^32 admits 2^32 chunks (0 to 2^32-1); a ceiling of 2^32-1 chunks stops one earlier. Off by one at the forced epoch roll; the recommended cap of 2^24 makes it unreachable in practice.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.3 32 bytes (caller-derived: sha256(stream_meta))
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.3 which MUST equal `SHA-256("ciris-edge:call-stream:v2" ‖ room ‖ publisher ‖ join_nonce)` with no length prefixes
note: The layout table gives one derivation of stream_id and the binding gives another, which a receiver re-derives and refuses on mismatch. "stream_meta" is defined nowhere. The binding rule is the enforced one.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 `evidence_refs[]` stays bare sha256.
side_b: DATA manifests/signed_object_vectors.json evidence_refs element "sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
note: Bare is meant as "no multihash or CID layer", but reads as an unprefixed 64-hex string. The vectors, CC 3.1.5 and the 3.3.13 field set ("digest sha256:<hex> ... == evidence_refs[]") carry the "sha256:" prefix. A producer writing bare hex and a consumer comparing against "sha256:<hex>" never match.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 [CC 5.3.2.5](part_5_transport_substrate.md) rules it for anything `evidence_refs[]` cites
side_b: CC 5.3.2.5 A blob cited only by a bare `evidence_refs[]` string has no declared size
note: CC 3.3.13 credits 5.3.2.5 with requiring a size on everything evidence_refs cites; 5.3.2.5 requires it only of a blob cited through a descriptor and gives the bare-string case the 1 MiB cap instead. A consumer built from 3.3.13 refuses a bare-cited blob for want of a size; one built from 5.3.2.5 fetches it under the cap.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 Registry key_ids are themselves hex fingerprints, not base64 pubkeys
side_b: CC 2.6.8 `fingerprint` = the first **10 base32 characters** (50 bits) of `sha256(ed25519_pubkey)`, lowercased
note: The reason given for the mandatory tag describes key ids as hex fingerprints; the key_id format is label plus a base32 fingerprint, and the same paragraph of 2.3.2.1 says so two sentences earlier. Only the older 64-hex ids fit the sentence. The MUST is unaffected.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1 against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**
side_b: CC 2.6.8 a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains
note: CC 2.3.2.1 limits the check to the two proof-of-possession doors and keeps a held key under a non-matching id; CC 2.6.8 binds every resolution, which refuses that held key. CC 2.6.8 then says a collision is "detected at registration and never at resolution", agreeing with 2.3.2.1 against its own MUST.

side_a: CC 3.1.2 Carries no version segment (`_meta.case_rule.version_segment.exempt`): the suffix is the hash.
side_b: CC 3.1.7 a tail on one is tolerated, never required
note: The row says the family carries none; CC 3.1.7 and the manifest note admit a tail, and the match vectors admit identity:canonical_binding:<hash>:v1. A matcher built from the row refuses the tailed form.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 is the token `federation_malformed_row` with one reason from this closed set
side_b: CC 3.1.9.7 is refused `federation_malformed_row` with reason `goal_meta_alignment_malformed`
note: The closed set of seven reasons in CC 2.6.1.7 holds neither goal_meta_alignment_malformed (CC 3.1.9.7) nor aggregate_source_duplicate (CC 6.1.1), both issued under the same token. A client that switches on the closed set meets a reason it must treat as unknown. CC 5.3.6.1 also cites federation_set_semantics_unsorted to CC 2.6.1.2; its home is 2.6.1.1.1.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 "nonce=" || base64url(rand_32_bytes) || "\n" ||
side_b: CC 2.6.1.1.1 every field documented as base64 MUST use the RFC 4648 §4 STANDARD alphabet, WITH padding
note: The four accord preimages (invoke, lifecycle, proposal, participation) write the nonce as base64url, with padding unstated, against the one base64 variant CC 2.6.1.1.1 pins "globally". If a verifier rebuilds the line from the 32 raw bytes, a padded and an unpadded encoder disagree and the holder's signature fails; if the nonce travels as the string the signer wrote, nothing diverges. The sections do not say which.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 The latch is idempotent, so a replayed or second row changes nothing.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.3 A resumption authorizes ending a *single named* `constitutional` halt, not resumption-in-general.
note: Two holders fire two halts (two ids) for one emergency. Under 4.2.1.1 the second row changes nothing: one latch, the first id, the first fuse. Under 4.2.1.3 and the confirmation rule ("names the halt by id") each halt is its own object. If the majority confirms the second id, a single-latch node sees a confirmation of a halt it never latched and lapses at the first fuse; a per-halt node stays paused. Likewise a resumption of the first id frees a single-latch node and leaves a per-halt node paused under the second. Neither section says which halt is "the currently-active" one when two have arrived.

side_a: CC 3.2 the halt latch **as it reaches this node** ([CC 4.2.1](part_4_composition_governance.md): a live accord edge at the halt's `asserted_at`)
side_b: CC 4.2.1 The signer-chosen `asserted_at` plays no part, as for the fuse
note: Ruled 2026-11-11 for the node's latch instant; CC 3.2's list of what a verdict reads still judges the edge at asserted_at. A node that cut its edge after a pre-signed row's asserted_at and before the row arrived is reached under 3.2 and not under 4.2.1.

side_a: CC 4.2 it reaches exactly those holding a live trust edge to the accord when it is fired
side_b: CC 4.2.1 at the instant the halt becomes active at that node
note: When it is fired is one instant for the federation; the home rule is each node's own latch instant. CC 4.2.6 repeats the first form ("no halt fired after the cut reaches that node"). CC 4.2.1 governs.

side_a: CC 4.2.6 within `halt_fuse_secs` of the halt, or the lone halt lapses
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 admitted at a node before that node's own fuse lapses
note: One table measures the confirmation window from "the halt", the other from each node's receipt on its own clock. A node that received the halt late admits a confirmation another node, measuring from the first publication, would treat as too late. CC 4.2.1.1 and the window-clock rule of CC 4.5.13 support per-node receipt.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 The nonce is single-use within `valid_until`.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 So a sealed row signed months earlier is live when published
note: The signed bytes carry valid_until and the duplicate rule is bounded by it, but no sentence says whether a halt published after its own valid_until fires. A pre-signed row kept sealed for months either needs a far-future valid_until or is dead on publication; one implementer checks it, another follows "asserted_at plays no part" and ignores both instants.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 `halt_fuse_secs` is a charter member ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) whose **absence means 86400**
side_b: DATA constitution/governance_policy.tsv accord_halt: window_secs 86400, window_class fuse_24h
note: The text makes the fuse a charter value with a default (CC 2.6.1.2: "an explicit value overrides"); the policy row and the CC 4.5.1 register ("lapses at 24 h") state the number as fixed. A kernel that reads the window from the policy table ignores a charter that sets 3600.

side_a: CC 4.2.1 `EmergencyShutdown CONSTITUTIONAL` (`IncidentSeverity::INCIDENT_CONSTITUTIONAL = 5`);
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 are the *severity* enum of the shutdown message, not a dimension token, and are outside R3
note: The list of what an accord signature is valid on names the halt by a message and severity enum; every other section names it as the row accord:invoke:constitutional:{halt_id} (CC 3.4.1), and CC 4.2.1.1 says the halt "begins and ends with the row". The enumeration never names the row, so read literally the registered halt row is outside it.

side_a: CC 3.2 the accord's roster-keyed asymmetry rides existing primitives + scope-isolation rules
side_b: CC 4.2 it is not an asymmetry: it is the piece that makes the relationship between a sentient maker and a sapient made thing symmetric
note: CC 3.2 still names the accord's power an asymmetry; CC 4.2 and CC 1.13.2 state it as the condition of symmetry. Same residue as C059 and C245, in a third place.

side_a: CC 4.2.1 Humanity-accord authority signs nothing outside this enumeration.
side_b: CC 3.4.1 The accord-holder verdict on an agent's human-dignity conduct, carried as `accord:human_dignity:v1` (`attested_key_id` = the agent scored)
note: The enumeration of CC 4.2.1 holds neither accord:human_dignity nor the accord heartbeat accord:lifecycle ("accord-holder self-attestation about the accord", CC 3.4.1); both are registered leaves only an accord_holder may emit, and transitions.json admits each on one holder's act. A verifier built from 4.2.1 refuses them as out of role; one built from the registry admits them. C051 records the same gap for the roster-change objects of CC 4.2.6.

side_a: CC 4.2.3 name the three holders' hybrid keys (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65), one per person
side_b: CC 4.5.1 a holder's primary and backup keys are one holder, under whichever of their keys is live
note: CC 4.2.3 seats one key per holder; CC 4.5.1 counts a holder under a primary or a backup key. No section says how a backup key is seated, pinned in the bundle or recognised by a verifier, and CC 4.2.6 gives recovery by a pre-committed rotation, never a standing second key. A halt or a sign-off signed by a backup key is honoured under 4.5.1 and refused under 4.2.3.

side_a: CC 3.2 halt, notify, drill, resumption, root conferral, pipeline blessing, the amendment sign-off and entrenched ratification
side_b: CC 4.2.1 the agent text manifest statement of [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.2); and
note: CC 3.2 restates the closed list of accord powers without the confirmation (accord:lifecycle:confirmed), the agent text manifest statement and the AccordCarrier announcement that CC 4.2.1 lists. A reader of 3.2 alone takes those three as outside the accord's role. CC 4.2.1 is the home.

side_a: CC 3.3.4 consensus_protocol_entrenched: true // replacement only via CC 4.2.1 ceremony
side_b: CC 4.2.3 consensus_protocol_entrenched: true // replacement runs the CC 4.2.6 roster-change ceremony
note: Two copies of one family record cite two sections for the replacement of a holder. CC 4.2.1 holds no replacement ceremony (its ceremonies confer a root and bless a pipeline); CC 4.2.6 holds the roster change. The member keys also differ in form (quoted placeholders against bracketed names).

side_a: CC 4.2.5 The three named human key holders hold `AccordCarrier` authority
side_b: CC 4.2.1.1 never a fixed 2-of-3: three holders is the seed, not the rule
note: CC 4.2.5 (and "naming your own three") still writes the roster as three; the rule is M of N over the standing roster with three as the seed. No count depends on the sentence.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.4 The perceptual-hash tripwire likewise fires at every scope-widening promotion
side_b: CC 4.5.7 Detection runs **only at the publish/share seam of enabled groups**
note: CC 1.13.3.4 and 3.1.3.4 make the tripwire unconditional at every widening; CC 4.5.7 makes the matcher an opt-in the group's moderate-holder enables per group, on a hash list the operator provisions, and CC 4.5.13 repeats "only at enabled groups' publish/share seam". A promotion into a group that has not enabled a list is hash-matched under the first and not under the second. Neither says whether the CSAM list is the always-on case.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.4 **substrate-protective perceptual-hash tripwire at every scope-*widening* promotion event**, never on the device, never inside a private cohort
side_b: CC 3.2 runs on the post exactly as it runs on a promotion into the Commons — never inside a private cohort, never on the device
note: A widening from self to family, or from family to a gated community, is a scope-widening promotion that lands inside a private cohort. "Every widening" (CC 3.1.3.4: "Every widening is an act on specific bytes ... each with its own emission and tripwire") matches it; "never inside a private cohort" and the next sentence of 1.13.3.4 (only a promotion into the Commons or a post into a public room is matched) do not. The Commons-or-public-room reading is the one the privacy position supports.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 The **sender canonicalises before hashing** — which is also what strips EXIF / XMP / ID3 / ICC — and the **node stores and forwards verbatim**.
side_b: CC 5.3.2.6 so every client renders only bytes the node's safe encoder produced
note: CC 3.3.13 puts re-encoding and metadata stripping on the sender before the hash and has the node forward verbatim; CC 5.3.2.6 puts a re-encode and strip pipeline on the receiving node and has clients render only its output, while its own table marks a verified Tier-A blob "render". A client that renders verified sender bytes follows the table; one that waits for a node rendition follows the pipeline sentence. Both keep the digest rule if the node output is a separate rendition.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 **without** adopting C2PA's binary manifest
side_b: CC 3.4.14 that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media
note: CC 3.3.13 says C2PA's manifest is not adopted ("verify-only enrichment on the node at most, later"); CC 3.4.14 requires the C2PA assertion at egress for generated media and requires it to ship with the first release that publishes any. They meet only if 3.3.13 is read as "not inside the mesh" and 3.4.14 as "at the egress boundary"; 3.3.13 does not say so.

side_a: CC 7.3.4 Where feasible and appropriate, embed cryptographic provenance watermarks adhering to recognized standards (e.g., C2PA)
side_b: CC 3.4.14 is normative **wherever generated media is published**
note: Part 7 leaves the provenance mark to feasibility; CC 3.4.14 makes it a MUST for generated media at every egress. CC 3.4.14 is the later and the specific rule.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10 # Producer-declared content_class is consultable but not authoritative — UI may show
side_b: CC 4.4.3.10 (class, _, prefs) if class in prefs.blocked_classes => Block
note: The comment says the producer's class is shown and the person chooses; the next line blocks on it outright. A gate built from the code hides the item; one built from the comment shows it with the claim beside it.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.10 `self < provider:{verifier_key}:adult < government:{credential_class}:adult`
side_b: CC 3.4.11 are the only shapes this Part registers
note: The ordering is written with a third segment ({verifier_key}, {credential_class}) the registered age_assurance:{level}:{band} shape does not have, and with `self` as a level, which CC 3.4.11 says it is not. See the wire finding on the MAY in CC 3.4.11: this is its second witness.

side_a: CC 3.3.3 **Typical cohort_scope**: `federation` (the disclosure IS the opt-in; non-private by design).
side_b: CC 2.1 The authoring default is the smallest scope
note: For a location proof the section names federation as the typical scope; the envelope rule and CC 1.13.3.4 make the smallest scope the authoring default and federation the opt-in. A client that pre-selects by 3.3.3 publishes a person's rough location to everyone unless they narrow it; one that follows 2.1 does the reverse. "Typical" is not a default, so a careful reader follows 2.1.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 User-private; always `cohort_scope: self`; promotable via
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3 promotion to community/global widens `cohort_scope` via the `supersedes` structural primitive
note: Always self and "promotion widens cohort_scope" both describe local_data. If the promoted row keeps sub_kind local_data it is not always self; if admission enforces "always self" the promotion must change the sub_kind, which neither section says.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.3 `self`, `family`, `community` or `affiliations` for a bounded cohort, **`federation` for Commons and `public` content**
side_b: CC 2.1 a closed set of seven
note: The custody rule lists five scopes for a report and refuses a report "whose scope is not its content's"; content at species or biosphere scope is admissible under CC 2.1 and has no line in the list. The equality rule covers it; the enumeration does not.

side_a: CC 2.1 One of `self`, `family`, `community`, `affiliations`, `species`, `biosphere`, `federation`
side_b: DATA formal/derivation/family_default_row.json placement: self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons (and "addressed" on two census families in manifests/family_model.json)
note: The text's placement axis is seven cohort scopes; the family model's placement column has four values and one extra. affiliations, species and biosphere have no value in the data, and "addressed" has no scope in the text. A kernel run on the column cannot place a row at three of the seven.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 `transport` (bootstrap peers, peer sideband) — MUST be emitted at `self`.
side_b: DATA manifests/family_model.json config:{scope} placement: any of the four, "signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text pins the admission and transport config leaves to self; the data cell for the family records no constraint. The cell is marked a gap, so the data is behind the text.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 The client holds no copy of its own.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 a consumer MAY resolve that id from a bundle it still holds
note: Adjacent sentences. The first forbids a client-held string table; the second permits resolving from one while a node lacks the locale. The second is a stated transition, so a careful reader takes the first as the end state.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A client renders an item with no node, from the data alone.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 **Every string the client shows is served by the node as a text reference,**
note: An item rendered with no node has no node to serve its strings, and the client "holds no copy of its own". Either the item carries its own text (then not every string is node-served) or it cannot be rendered before a node exists.
